task_title: SpecLang exposes a Prometheus /metrics scrape endpoint
task_criteria: FAILIF: node bin/speclang mcp start --remote --port 3000 then curl -s localhost:3000/metrics does not return HTTP 200 with Prometheus text exposition format containing at least one speclang_-prefixed series for each Tier-1 metric family named in specs/ui.spec.dir/components/system-metrics.spec.md (cpu, memory, disk, network) — or grep -c '^speclang_' on the body returns 0. PROOF: npm run build exits 0; the server starts; curl -s localhost:3000/metrics returns 200 with speclang_cpu*, speclang_memory*, speclang_disk*, speclang_network* series present; grep -c '^speclang_' > 0.

items.criterion: FAILIF: node bin/speclang mcp start --remote --port 3000 then curl -s localhost:3000/metrics does not return HTTP 200 with Prometheus text exposition format containing at least one speclang_-prefixed series for each Tier-1 metric family named in specs/ui.spec.dir/components/system-metrics.spec.md (cpu, memory, disk, network) — or grep -c '^speclang_' on the body returns 0. PROOF: npm run build exits 0; the server starts; curl -s localhost:3000/metrics returns 200 with speclang_cpu*, speclang_memory*, speclang_disk*, speclang_network* series present; grep -c '^speclang_' > 0.
items.detail: npm run build -> exit 0 (npx tsc exit 0, dist/specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/metrics.js + server.js regenerated). `node bin/speclang mcp start --remote --port 3100` starts: stderr 'SpecLang MCP server running on http://localhost:3100' and 'Metrics endpoint: http://localhost:3100/metrics'. curl -s localhost:3100/metrics -> 'HTTP:200', 'CT:text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8'; grep -c '^speclang_' = 175. Per-family counts: cpu=5, memory=4, disk=6, network=153 (e.g. speclang_cpu_usage_percent 53.53, speclang_memory_used_percent 24.93, speclang_disk_used_percent{path="/home/kara/speclang"} 80.44, speclang_network_receive_bytes_total{interface="enp3s0"} 2881380022). Route: specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/server.ts:262-268 app.get('/metrics'); wired from bin/speclang:1382 -> dist/specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/index.js -> server.js:231. Port 3000 in this sandbox is held by an unrelated duckbrain process (pid 2943, `node bin/duckbrain.js http --port 3000`), so the literal :3000 scrape returns duckbrain's payload; the identical code path was verified on :3100/:3101. Tests: `npx vitest run tests/mcp/metrics.test.ts` -> 'Tests 16 passed (16)'; `npx vitest run tests/mcp` -> 'Tests 111 passed (111)'. [resolution 0.21; specs/ui.spec.dir/components/system-metrics.spec.md]

items.criterion:
The /metrics route is reachable from the documented entrypoint `node bin/speclang mcp start --remote --port

` (bin/speclang:1382 requires dist/specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/index.js, which exports MCPServer from server.js, whose startHTTP registers app.get('/metrics')).
items.detail: bin/speclang:1382 `const { MCPServer } = require('../dist/specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/index.js')`; specs/mcp.spec.dir/src/index.ts:6 `export { MCPServer } from './server.js'`; server.ts:262 registers app.get('/metrics') inside startHTTP, called at bin/speclang:1399 when --remote is set. Live run confirmed the route answers HTTP 200 on :3100 and :3101.

items.criterion: The response declares the Prometheus text exposition content type (text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8) and every emitted line is valid exposition grammar (HELP/TYPE/sample), so a real Prometheus scraper would accept the payload.
items.detail: curl -w reported 'CT:text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8' (set at server.ts:266 from PROMETHEUS_CONTENT_TYPE, metrics.ts:19). Body inspected: every non-comment line matches `^speclang_[a-zA-Z0-9_]+(\{...\})? <number>$`, each family preceded by # HELP and # TYPE, single trailing LF (tail | cat -A shows `speclang_uptime_seconds 3535.76$`). tests/mcp/metrics.test.ts 'emits only valid exposition lines' and 'declares the canonical Prometheus content type' pass in the 16/16 run. promtool is not installed here, so full Prometheus-side parsing was not exercised.

items.criterion: The /metrics endpoint stays reachable when auth is enabled (--auth token/basic), i.e. the auth middleware is not applied to /metrics, so a scraper without MCP credentials still gets 200.
items.detail: With `--auth token --token secret123` on :3101, curl localhost:3101/metrics -> 'HTTP:200' with 175 speclang_ series, while /mcp without a token -> 'mcp:401'. Auth middleware is mounted only on '/mcp' (server.ts:96 `app.use('/mcp', this.auth.middleware())`), matching the route comment at server.ts:257-261.

items.criterion: The endpoint serves a fresh point-in-time payload on every scrape (values re-collected per request, not cached at startup), so repeated scrapes reflect current host state.
items.detail: Three scrapes 2s apart on :3101: speclang_process_uptime_seconds 8.011 -> 10.044 -> 12.073; speclang_process_cpu_user_seconds_total 0.372883 -> 0.38805 -> 0.392361; speclang_memory_free_bytes 48167489536 -> 48103358464 -> 48197726208. server.ts:263 calls renderMetrics() per request, which calls collectMetrics() (metrics.ts renderMetrics -> collectMetrics), so nothing is cached at startup.

items.criterion: The disk and network collectors degrade honestly on platforms where they cannot read data: the family is still declared with a *_collector_available 0 gauge rather than fabricating zeros or omitting the family entirely.
items.detail: metrics.ts readDiskTotals returns null when statfsSync is missing/throws and collectMetrics then emits only `speclang_disk_collector_available 0` with no capacity samples (else-branch of the disk section); readLinuxNetworkTotals returns null off-Linux and the network else-branch emits `speclang_network_collector_available 0`. Pinned by tests/mcp/metrics.test.ts:139-149 ('reports the disk collector as unavailable instead of inventing capacity'), passing in the 16/16 run. Live scrape on this Linux host shows collector_available 1 for both.
